## p145 A — HVC fragment with its first part missing

**Edition context:** p145 A — HVC fragment with its first part missing.

<a id="edition-cases-open-p145-a-p145-a--hvc-fragment-with-its-first-part-missing"></a>



**State: OPEN.** Source transcription and review: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

This surviving fragment remains unread. The source says “missed first part” and gives no transmitted length. Its 192 received slots therefore cannot be assumed to be the complete transposition frame.

<a id="edition-cases-open-p145-a-boundaries-and-uncertainty"></a>

### Boundaries and uncertainty

The page heading is `6th NOVEMBER, 1918`; the reception header says
November 7th at 02.28 a.m. Neither date is silently corrected.

The nine-dash mark in the left margin occupies the message-designator
column. It is metadata, not an extra nine cipher slots. The first cipher
group is the separate five-dash run in the body column. Those five erasures
and all 187 observed coordinates are retained. The final `AD` is a two-symbol
cipher group; the following `NF HVC U` is clear metadata outside the body.

“Missed first part” does not give a number of missing coordinates or prove
that this fragment is the suffix of one longer encrypted block. A model
that adds a prefix must state its length and source map explicitly.

<a id="edition-cases-open-p145-a-research-leads"></a>

### Research leads

- Compare the reception date with the `Nov4-6` and `Nov7-9` period keys without assuming that the page heading establishes the key.
- Look for another reception or part label carrying the HVC route and the same observed suffix; an independently printed copy would constrain frame length more strongly than language scoring.
- Test complete-fragment and missing-prefix models separately. Keep the five printed erasures distinct from any unprinted coordinates introduced by a hypothesis.

These are research directions, not accepted decipherments. A failed search
under one key or loss model does not exclude other source-supported models.

<a id="edition-cases-open-p145-a-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence and reproduction

The [machine-readable source record](../../experiments/open_source_records/inputs.json)
retains the original audit metadata, exact source rows, annotation positions
and crop recipe. The [source-only verifier](../../experiments/open_source_records/verify.py)
checks the case transcription, literal digest, native counts and crop pixels;
it produces no plaintext certificate. The [21-source audit](../../docs/source-gap-audit.md)

```sh

```

## 6 November Ringbahn-key instruction: a second three-part witness

<a id="november-6-ringbahn-key-instruction-a-second-three-part-witness"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p145 B1, p145 B2, p145 B3.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-ringbahn-key-witnesses-november-6-ringbahn-key-instruction-a-second-three-part-witness"></a>



**Third reception restored.** The [p187 B1 fragment](187.md#edition-cases-radio-nov13-ringbahn-retransmission) adds a separately received witness with an exact origin map for every restored coordinate.

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p145 supplies three additional physical witnesses of the instruction
already read in the [p211 lower-B edition](211.md#edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule). They say to
keep the November Ringbahn keys, postpone the December keys, and use the
10 November key for 1 December through the 30 November key for 21 December.
These are the stated instructions; implementation by every station is not
inferred.

The source has **531 typed coordinates**, with a visibly four-symbol group
in part 2 against its advertised length. The declared 532-slot frames give
**266 positions**, **265 fixed raw**. The complete candidates use **5 observed
coordinate substitutions** and **1 fill in the hypothesized added slot**.
Every proposed changed plaintext position is directly supported by a fixed
raw position in the independently inspected p211 source. Conversely, the
p145 raw text directly supports all four earlier p211 word repairs.

### Dates and source identity

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal p145 headers:**

```text
6th NOVEMBER, 1918.
B) WAU (KOW RVA) NKJ (IWE RTS) ASO v LP (02.53 a.m., November 7th)
SS DD 2230 (6/11) 3 TEILE
1 TL RICHI-214
2 TL RICHI-184
3 TL RICHI-134
```

</details>

The [p211 source crop](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p211_selected.png)
instead has a **19 November** heading and **22 November** receipt, with
`FUER POT COS VON LP SS DD 2230 3 TLE`. Both copies decode under the unchanged
published **Nov4–6** key. The date layers remain as printed. No date is
rewritten to fit the cipher period or the December instruction.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov6-ringbahn-key-witnesses-cross-copy-repair-support-and-preserved-disagreements"></a>

### Cross-copy repair support and preserved disagreements

All five possible insertions within the short `XFVA` group are priced against
the independently read p211 part 2:

| Source boundary | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Added value |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 30 | 6 | X |
| 31 | 5 | F |
| 32 | 4 | V |
| 33 | 3 | F |
| 34 | 4 | A |

The boundary-33 frame has the least observed-coordinate cost within this
explicit five-alignment family. The three substitutions concern source
indices **44, 87 and 127**. This comparison uses an actual copy, not a text
selected solely for a higher language score; it still does not identify the
historical stage at which the coordinate was lost.

The reverse support is also exact. In p145 part 1, the unedited letters at
plaintext indices **9, 19 and 67** support the p211 proposals `RINGBAHN`,
`SCHLUESSEL` and `DEZEMBER`. In p145 part 3, unedited position **10** supports
the p211 `DREISSIGSTER` fill. Both source transcriptions remain available;
these observations do not merge the physical records.

The reference labels remain different. p145 has literal `NACHRCHEFXG` in
part 1 and `NACHRCHEFX4` in part 3; the p211 outputs have `NACHRCHEFX4` and
`NACHRCHEFZ4`. Those labels are **not regularized**, even though the schedule
words agree. The numerical fields `B848727` and `47857` likewise stay literal.

**Meaning:** The schedule itself is the already established instruction to
reuse November key dates for the beginning of December. These p145 witnesses
provide independent character-level support for the text, recover a short
source group, and expose the differing date and reference layers. They add
no claim about the behavior of any station or the key of a particular
December ciphertext.
